facts.subject: Escape crystal (Hardcore Worlds)
facts.value: 1 free at start; Death sells more for 10,000 coins
facts.statement: Every Hardcore Worlds character starts with one free escape crystal, and Death sells more for 10,000 coins each (also sold by Rick at the Wizards' Tower and the Mysterious Stranger in Ver Sinhaza).
facts.caveat: The value (1 free, 10,000 coins from Death) is verified. The researcher's added description 'an auto-escape safety tool relevant to risky courses' is NOT supported by what I fetched: the wiki describes the teleport/auto-AFK teleport as working out of a listed set of activities (Barbarian Assault, Chambers of Xeric, Inferno, Pest Control, Theatre of Blood, TzHaar-Ket-Rak's Challenges, Tombs of Amascut, and the Gauntlet), and when equipped it acts like a ring of life (which disables the activity teleport). It does not activate while the player is moving, and its teleport works only up to level 30 Wilderness. Do not present it as an Agility-course safety net without a threat-desk fact (see RFI). New content.

I re-fetched the rewards of all 17 quests: fixed Agility XP only from The Writing's on the Wall; no fixed Defence XP anywhere. facts.subject: Graveyard Agility course
facts.value: 65-80 Agility; hybrid course (about two thirds rooftop-style, one third choice of AFK ~20-30s or one-tick high-intensity obstacles)
facts.statement: The Graveyard Agility course is aimed at players with 65-80 Agility. Jagex's 14 Sep blog described it as about two thirds traditional rooftop-style obstacles and one third a choice between slow AFK obstacles (about 20-30 seconds) and intense obstacles.
facts.caveat: UPCOMING design intent, not release fact. The 65-80 target is in the T1 Summer Campfire post. The 'two thirds rooftop' wording is in the 14 Sep T1 blog, but Jagex's 18 Sep update on the same page walks it back ('We feel we did an injustice describing the course has having two thirds of it similar to rooftops') and says the AFK option may be made more consistent with reduced XP. T1 describes it as a dark underwater cavern where you 'dodge debris, leap across half-sunken wreckage and try to stay above water'; its Hardcore Worlds danger is unknown until release. Never a route step.

[18 Sep update:] We feel we did an injustice describing the course has having two thirds of it similar to rooftops. While you could argue it has the potential to be as passive as rooftops, the onus is ultimately on the player.

facts.subject: Colossal Wyrm Agility Course
facts.statement: Post-12-August-2026 Wyrm XP per lap is unconfirmed. The course page (flagged {{Obsolete}} for the 12 Aug 2026 changes) states 633 basic / 1,053.6 advanced, but its own basic obstacle table sums to 601.6 (7 x 37.2 + 341.2); the advanced table sums to 1,053.6. The Agility skill page still gives the pre-rework 504.1 / 749.6. Jagex's T1 notes give no per-lap numbers.
facts.caveat: Not marked STALE: the course page has not changed since the researcher's revid 15388138 (it is still the current revision), so the researcher's figure is what the page says. It is DISPUTED because sources disagree (prose vs table vs skill page) and the page is self-flagged out of date. Planners must not compute laps from per-lap XP; use the XP/hour fact F-1049.

facts.subject: Colossal Wyrm Agility Course
facts.statement: The Colossal Wyrm course gives up to about 31,000 XP/h on the basic route and about 42,000-43,000 XP/h on the advanced route.
facts.caveat: Ceilings assuming ideal post-rework lap times (basic 1:07.8, advanced 1:22.8, 3.6 s downtime); obstacles cannot be failed so only attentiveness matters. Supported by the T1 note that XP/h is 'roughly the same' after the 12 Aug 2026 change. The course page carries an {{Obsolete}} banner; the Agility skill page's section (which still shows pre-rework per-lap XP) says up to 44,000 for advanced, so treat 43,000 as the ceiling, not a typical rate. Realistic attentive play will be lower.

facts.subject: Hallowed Sepulchre
facts.statement: Sepulchre floors give 575/925/1,600/2,875/5,725 XP, so a run to Floors 1/2/3/4/5 gives 575/1,500/3,100/5,975/11,700 XP in total.
facts.caveat: Two separately maintained wiki tables agree. Treasure encounters add 100/100/150/150/160 XP per floor (Sepulchre page); Floor 2 north pillars can give 935.

facts.subject: Hallowed Sepulchre
facts.statement: Sepulchre runs give about 40,000-56,300 XP/h through Floor 2, 63,000-71,700 through Floor 3, 73,000-81,000 through Floor 4 and 85,800-98,500 through Floor 5; the absolute cap is about 102,000-108,000.
facts.caveat: High intensity; requires practice. Ranges span two wiki tables: Sepulchre page 'realistic' looting / no-looting (F2 40,000/50,000; F3 63,000/71,700; F4 73,000/81,000; F5 90,000/98,500) and the training table, which assumes good practice and a private instance (200 hallowed marks): F2 56,300, F3 68,900, F4 79,700 (75,000 looting), F5 98,500 (85,800 looting). Floor 1 is 30,000-45,000. Expect lower while learning. Requires Sins of the Father (F-1054).

sources.title: Agility training

value.combat_area: singles-plus, player killers can attack at any time

facts.statement: The Wilderness course sits in Wilderness levels 50-56 in a singles-plus combat area where player killers can attack at any time, even mid-combat; level 18 and 25 skeletons roam the course and the dungeon below.

facts.caveat: Assumes ~45 s laps including fails (obstacles can fail even at 99), tickets redeemed in batches of 101+ (needs about 2 hours of play), and no player-killer disruption. The training page lists this course for 47-62 only. Rates fall, and risk rises, if PKers are active.

facts.statement: The Fremennik Trials requires fighting Koschei the deathless in an instance with no armour, weapons or spells. Food, prayer, god books and jewellery are allowed. His four forms have 30/50/70/255 HP and max hits of 3/5/7/1. The wiki says dying to any form is safe for regular hardcore ironmen, but that hardcore group ironmen must be concerned about dying in the first three forms. Hardcore Worlds uses the HGIM death ruleset, so forms 1-3 must be treated as potentially run-ending. The 4th-form death is scripted.
facts.caveat: Resolves the researcher's doubt: the 4th-form max hit of 1 is not an anomaly. That form attacks every game tick (0.6 s) for exactly 1, drains prayer, and has 255 HP. The third form has a 10-minute time limit. A ring of life sends you back to spawn and resets him to form 1. If he stays idle too long he resets to form 1. On HW, death safety for forms 1-3 needs a Threat-desk ruling (RFI-01 already open).

sources.title: Koschei the deathless
sources.quote: Dying to any of his forms are safe deaths (including for [[Hardcore ironmen]]), though players must die to his fourth form (or defeat it) to get the vote. Only [[Hardcore group ironmen]] need to be concerned about dying to the first three forms, as dying to the fourth form is a scripted safe death.

facts.value: flashbacks block teleport
facts.statement: Once an Icthlarin's Little Helper flashback starts, you cannot teleport away until you finish it or die. You can walk back to the entrance, or log out and back in to be placed outside the pyramid.

facts.statement: The Ape Atoll Agility Course needs Agility 48 (cannot be boosted), partial completion of Monkey Madness I up to Chapter 2, and a small or medium ninja monkey greegree or the Kruk greegree worn. The Jungle Demon fight is not needed for course access.
facts.caveat: Obstacles (all except the stepping stones and the last tropical tree) can be failed for small damage until Agility 75. Trying an obstacle without a ninja or Kruk greegree fails it and deals damage.

sources.title: Ape Atoll Agility Course

Access to this course requires partial completion of [[Monkey Madness I]], up to Chapter 2. To use the agility course, the player has to wear either the [[Ninja monkey greegree (small)|small]] or [[Ninja monkey greegree (medium)|medium-sized]] ninja monkey greegree or the [[Kruk monkey greegree]].

facts.subject: Ape Atoll Agility Course
facts.statement: The Ape Atoll Agility Course gives 580 Agility XP per completed lap.
facts.caveat: The XP/h figures on the page disagree with each other: the intro says up to 55,200/h and 40,000-50,000/h at lower levels; the rates section says 55,100/h at 75+ (95 laps of 63 ticks) and 40,000-45,000/h at lower levels. Rates belong to the Methods desk; only 580/lap is verified here.

sources.title: Ape Atoll Agility Course
sources.quote: The agility course rewards 580 [[Agility]] [[experience]] per completed lap. ... At level 75 and higher, expect to be able to complete a maximum of 95 laps per hour (63 [[Game tick|ticks]] per lap), resulting in 55,100 [[Agility]] experience per hour. At lower [[Agility]] levels, expect to get around 40,000–45,000

facts.subject: Monkey Madness I
facts.value: kill a ninja monkey on Ape Atoll for bones + monkey talisman, made by Zooknock
facts.statement: Zooknock makes each greegree from a monkey talisman plus the bones (or corpse) of the matching monkey. The ninja monkey greegree, needed for the Ape Atoll course, requires killing a ninja monkey. Extra talismans come from the monkey child, or cost 1,000 coins at Tutab's Magical Market once you can take monkey form.
facts.caveat: Ninja monkey combat stats were not researched (raised as an RFI to the Threat desk). Bringing the bones to Zooknock means another run through the Ape Atoll Dungeon tunnel (see F-2088).

sources.title: Monkey Madness I
sources.quote: Each of these requires one talisman ... You must kill one of each of the following: ... |{{Ilink|Ninja monkey greegree|txt=Ninja monkey|pic=Ninja monkey greegree (medium)}} ... '''use''' the [[monkey talisman]] and all monkey bones (or corpses) on [[Zooknock]].

facts.subject: Monkey Madness I
facts.statement: Monkey Madness I's only Defence XP comes from Daero's optional training after the quest: 35,000 to Attack and Defence and 20,000 to Strength and Hitpoints, or the reverse. Since 30 November 2022 you can return to Ape Atoll without accepting the training. A zerker can therefore take 0 Defence XP. If the training is accepted, Defence gets at least 20,000 (35,000 = level 39 by tools/xp.py).
facts.caveat: Build-critical: the route must say to decline (ignore) Daero's training. Declining means heavy ballistae cannot be used later, which does not affect Agility. Confirmed by a Jagex T1 post.

sources.title: Monkey Madness I
sources.quote: '''Note:''' while it was previously impossible to return to Ape Atoll after quest completion without receiving experience from Daero, an [[Update:The Garden of Death & More#Poll 77 Changes|update]] in November 2022 now allows the training to be ignored before returning.

sources.title: Update:The Garden of Death & More
sources.quote: '''Poll 77 Changes''' * Players can now get back to Ape Atoll without accepting Daero's Training, after completing Monkey Madness I.

facts.statement: Monkey Madness I's final fight is the Jungle Demon (level 195, max hit 32 with both magic and melee; his melee reaches two squares). Protection prayers reduce all his damage to zero. There is a safespot across a bridge, and you must land the final blow yourself.
facts.caveat: Danger-critical. A max hit of 32 is two thirds of the owner's 48 HP. Wearing the sigil starts the fight from anywhere. 'Reclaim the sigil from Death's Office' assumes a death, which is run-ending on HW. Not needed for the Agility course.

facts.statement: Monkey Madness I Chapter 2 (needed for the Ape Atoll course) runs through a long, tight multi-combat tunnel. It has 30 accurate monkey zombies (max 7) and 17 skeletons (max 12), plus traps: floor spikes (7.5% of current HP), a rock trap (20%) and falling rocks (4% every 15 s). Earlier, the Ape Atoll jail guards punch for 10-20.
facts.caveat: The dungeon map lists the monkey zombies as level 98 and the skeletons as level 142. Running through takes at least three minutes. Protect from Melee (Prayer 43; the owner has 44) is the listed counter. The trip is repeated to bring the ninja monkey bones to Zooknock.

facts.subject: Werewolf Agility Course
facts.statement: The Werewolf Agility Course needs Agility 60, completion of Creature of Fenkenstrain, and the Ring of Charos worn to use the trapdoor.
facts.caveat: The page does not say whether the 60 Agility requirement is boostable.

sources.title: Werewolf Agility Course
sources.quote: The '''Werewolf Agility course''' is an Agility training area located near [[Canifis]], available to players with level 60 [[Agility]]. Access to this course requires completion of [[Creature of Fenkenstrain]]. To access the Agility course, the player has to wear a [[Ring of Charos]]

facts.subject: Werewolf Agility Course
facts.value: can hit over 30 damage
facts.statement: On the Werewolf Agility Course the deathslide is the only obstacle that can be failed. A fall can deal over 30 damage, which does not scale with Hitpoints, and it is the only Agility obstacle that can deal damage past the player's Hitpoints. Higher Agility and Strength and lower weight improve success; with Agility and Strength 80+ and weight 2 kg or less it never fails.
facts.caveat: Danger-critical for a 48-HP Hardcore Worlds character: a deathslide fail can kill. The owner's Strength is 32 (far from 80). No head-slot item may be worn on the deathslide. The Threat desk must rate this before routing.

sources.title: Werewolf Agility Course
sources.quote: The deathslide is the only obstacle that can be failed by the player, which can hit over 30 damage. ... A fall can deal upwards of 30 damage and does NOT scale with [[Hitpoints]], so players with low HP are at risk of [[death]]. ... *The deathslide is the only agility obstacle that can do damage past the player's [[Hitpoints]].

facts.subject: Darkness of Hallowvale
facts.statement: Darkness of Hallowvale's tome of experience grants 2,000 XP to any three skills at level 30 or over (the same skill may be chosen), i.e. up to 6,000 Agility XP on top of the fixed 7,000 Agility XP.
facts.caveat: Zerker build: the prerequisite chain (In Aid of the Myreque <- In Search of the Myreque <- Nature Spirit) carries fixed Defence XP of 2,000 + 600 + 2,000 = 4,600 per the wiki Quest experience rewards Defence table; none of those three are in the owner's quest list. The quest itself also needs Strength 40 and Crafting 32 (both unboostable) and Mining 20; the owner has Strength 32 and Crafting 21. The tome must never be read into Defence.

facts.subject: The Graveyard
facts.statement: The Graveyard is announced to unlock an Agility 65 hybrid course aimed at Agility 65-80. Jagex projected 65,000-75,000 XP/h at high intensity and about 55,000-60,000 XP/h on the slower route, with the course meant to be the best mark-of-grace source when played at high intensity.
facts.caveat: Unreleased; rates were 'subject to change'. In a later update in the same blog, Jagex said the high-intensity figures assume tick-perfect play, real rates 'will be lower than this for most players' and 'likely comparable to Ardougne rooftops', and that it may reduce XP on the AFK option. Ardougne rooftops will still give more marks than the Graveyard's low-intensity option. Re-verify actual rates after the 2026-11-25 release.

sources.title: Update:The Graveyard - Rewards Blog
sources.quote: At the top end, you can expect to achieve 65,000 - 75,000 Agility XP per hour. ... If you're taking the slower route, you can expect around 55,000 - 60,000 Agility XP per hour.

sources.title: Update:The Graveyard - Rewards Blog
sources.quote: We'd also like to clarify that the rates we’ve shared for high-intensity Graveyard assume tick-perfect gameplay, which is difficult to maintain consistently in practice. In reality, it will be lower than this for most players. Graveyard's high-intensity option will likely be comparable to Ardougne rooftops.

facts.subject: Seers' Village Rooftop Course
facts.statement: A perfect Seers' rooftop lap takes 73 ticks (43.8 s), giving at most about 46,600 XP/h (~81 laps); with the Seers' bank teleport (about 37 s per lap) the maximum is about 56,000 XP/h (~97 laps). Each lap gives 570 XP.
facts.caveat: These are theoretical maximums with no failures; the wiki estimates about 75 s per lap at 60-65 and about 55 s later because of failures. The 56,000 figure needs the hard Kandarin Diary, which this zerker can never finish.

facts.subject: Owner's character (brief stats)
facts.statement: My own recomputation from the brief's stats (Def 1, HP 48, Prayer 44, Atk 44, Str 32, Ranged 56, Magic 44) gives base = (1+48+22)/4 = 17.75. Ranged = 0.325 x floor(56 x 1.5) = 0.325 x 84 = 27.3, melee = 0.325 x 76 = 24.7, magic = 0.325 x 66 = 21.45. Combat = floor(17.75 + 27.3) = floor(45.05) = 45. This matches the Director's correction (ledger seq 49).

sources.title: Combat level
sources.quote: \text{Final} &= \lfloor \text{Base} + \textrm{max}(\text{Melee}, \text{Range}, \text{Mage}) \rfloor

facts.subject: Level-based monster aggression
facts.value: aggressive if player combat level <= 2 x monster level; vs combat 45 every level-based aggressive monster of level 23+ attacks
facts.statement: Level-based aggressive monsters attack players whose combat level is at most twice their own. At combat 45 (the Director's figure), any such monster of level 23 or higher attacks (2 x 23 = 46 >= 45; 2 x 22 = 44 < 45). Monsters of level 63+ attack every player.

sources.title: Aggressiveness
sources.quote: When aggressiveness is based on combat level, an aggressive monster will attack a player whose combat level is less than or equal to twice the monster's level.

facts.subject: Monster aggression tolerance
facts.value: aggressive monsters become tolerant after 10 minutes in the area; leaving and returning resets it
facts.statement: Aggressive monsters become tolerant after the player spends 10 minutes nearby. Leaving and returning resets this, and so does returning from a random event. Logging out or hopping does not. Most Wilderness monsters are aggressive regardless of level, and some monsters never become tolerant (for example the WAC surface skeletons, F-3034).

sources.title: Aggressiveness
sources.quote: After a player spends 10 minutes in the vicinity of aggressive monsters, the monsters will become [[tolerant]] of the player and become passive. However, if the player leaves the area and then returns, the monsters there become aggressive again.

facts.subject: Kharidian Desert (Agility Pyramid, desert travel)
facts.statement: Outside towns, desert heat deals 1-10 damage every 24-132 seconds (90 by default; armour shortens it) unless a waterskin dose is drunk. Towns such as Pollnivneach, and open dialogue boxes, are exempt. The 90 s base is backed by a cited Jagex Mod Ash statement (150 ticks).

sources.title: Desert heat
sources.quote: For every 24-132 seconds (depending on armour worn) that a player spends in the desert, they will take 1-10 damage. [...] Players are not affected by desert heat while they are within the boundaries of towns or while a dialogue box is open. The default interval between damage is 90 seconds.

facts.subject: Hallowed Sepulchre
facts.value: small per trap hit, per-floor values not documented
facts.statement: Running into a trap usually teleports the player back to just before it and deals 'a small amount of damage' unless a hallowed ring is worn. The traps are wizard-statue fire, knight-statue swords and crossbowman-statue bolts. The wiki says deeper floors' traps are faster or doubled, but gives no damage numbers.
facts.caveat: No damage figure exists on the pinned wiki pages, and a web search found none on other sources. Planners must not invent numbers. Use the 70 HP recommendation (F-3056) as the only guidance.

sources.title: Hallowed Sepulchre
sources.quote: In most cases, running into a trap will teleport the player to a location just before the trap on the path, costing the player time. This deals a small amount of damage unless the [[hallowed ring]] is equipped.

facts.statement: Priest statues summon lightning in a 3x3 chequerboard that briefly stuns the player instead of dealing damage, leaving them immobile and open to other traps.

sources.title: Hallowed Sepulchre
sources.quote: * [[Priest statue]] - Statues that summon lightning in a 3x3 chequerboard pattern which stuns the player briefly instead of inflicting damage, however this leaves the player immobile and vulnerable to other traps.

facts.subject: Hallowed Sepulchre: coffins
facts.value: failing to loot a coffin poisons the player (2-damage poison per Strategies)
facts.statement: A failed coffin loot (66 Thieving, boostable) poisons the player. A lockpick, or better the strange old lockpick, lowers the failure chance.
facts.caveat: The 2-damage figure is an inference. The Coffin page gives no poison strength, and the Strategies page mentions '2-damage poison' only in a footnote about curing with a prayer book; it does not state the coffin poison's starting damage. Bring antipoison regardless.

sources.title: Coffin (Hallowed Sepulchre)

facts.subject: Hallowed ring

facts.statement: Computed: at Agility 57 and 0 kg, drain is 60*(1-57/300) = 48.6 units/tick, so 100% lasts about 206 ticks (about 2 min 4 s) of continuous running; with a stamina effect (floor of 0.3x = 14 units/tick) about 714 ticks (about 7 min 8 s).

sources.title: Energy
sources.quote: :<math> UnitsLost = \left\lfloor 60 + \frac{67 \,\times\, \text{clamp}_{[0,64]}(\text{weight})}{64} \right\rfloor \times (1 - \frac{\text{agility}}{300})</math>

sources.title: Energy
sources.quote: With the stamina potion effect, a player's run energy depletion rate is reduced to <math display="inline">\lfloor 0.3 * UnitsLost \rfloor</math>.

sources.title: Energy
sources.quote: Therefore, at a weight of 0kg it will always take between 170 ticks, or 102 seconds, (at level 1 Agility) and 250 ticks, or 150 seconds, (at level 99 Agility) for run energy to be fully depleted from 100%.{{Fact|Values may differ if UnitsLost isn't actually floored. Should also be tested if it is off by 1 tick due to how run into walk works once energy fully depletes.}}

facts.caveat: Rounding is unconfirmed (wiki {{Fact}} tag). The wiki's own worked example (170 ticks at level 1, 250 at 99) only reproduces if UnitsLost is floored to an integer; under that convention level 57 gives 48 units/tick and about 209 ticks (2 min 5 s), not 206. Treat no-stamina time as 206-209 ticks. With stamina both conventions give 14 units/tick and about 714 ticks. Ignores obstacle energy gains. Cited revision re-fetched and the current revision fetched the same day: the current revision is the cited one (no change).

facts.subject: Camelot Teleport

facts.statement: The Camelot Teleport spell needs 45 Magic (owner has 44) and lands at Camelot's front gate; moving it to Seers' bank needs the hard Kandarin diary (owner has none).

sources.title: Camelot Teleport

sources.title: Camelot Teleport

sources.title: Camelot Teleport
sources.quote: After completing the [[Hard Kandarin Diary|Kandarin Hard tasks]], you may switch the location of the teleport to [[Seers' Village bank]] by right-clicking the spell and choosing Toggle-location.

facts.subject: Camelot teleport (tablet)
facts.value: GE-tradeable; usable without the Magic level
facts.statement: Camelot teleport tablets are GE-tradeable and can be used without the Magic level, so the owner can reach Seers' with tablets now.

sources.title: Camelot teleport (tablet)
sources.quote: As with all tablets, the user does not need to have the relevant Magic level to use this tablet.

facts.subject: Pollnivneach
facts.value: only house teleport or a redirected house tablet teleports directly
facts.statement: The only direct teleports to Pollnivneach are a house teleport (house there) or the Pollnivneach redirected tablet; otherwise the magic carpet is used.

sources.title: Pollnivneach teleport
sources.quote: This tablet is the only method (outside of a normal [[House Teleport]] with a [[POH|house]] in Pollnivneach) of teleporting directly to Pollnivneach.

sources.title: Pollnivneach
sources.quote: If a player's house portal is in Pollnivneach, they may use the [[house teleport]] spell to reach the portal, thus bringing them to Pollnivneach. The POH Portals option on the [[Max cape]] can also teleport the player to the Pollnivneach house portal.

facts.caveat: The Pollnivneach town page adds the Max cape POH-portal option (not available to the owner). Fairy ring BIQ lands near Shantay Pass, not in town. House teleport into a POH: POH deaths are UNSAFE on Hardcore Worlds. Cited revision re-fetched and the current revision fetched the same day: the current revision is the cited one (no change).

facts.subject: Pollnivneach teleport
facts.value: untradeable; made from a teleport-to-house tablet plus a scroll of redirection at 20 Construction
facts.statement: The Pollnivneach teleport tablet is untradeable and made by using a scroll of redirection on a teleport-to-house tablet at 20 Construction (owner has 23).

sources.title: Pollnivneach teleport
sources.quote: |tradeable = No

sources.title: Pollnivneach teleport
sources.quote: It can be created at level 20 [[Construction]] by using a [[scroll of redirection]] on a [[teleport to house]] tablet.

facts.subject: Scroll of Redirection
facts.value: Nightmare Zone reward shop only, 775 points; untradeable
facts.statement: Scrolls of redirection come only from the Nightmare Zone reward shop (775 points each) and are untradeable; NMZ is an unsafe death on Hardcore Worlds, so redirected Pollnivneach/Rellekka tablets are not a safe option.

sources.title: Scroll of Redirection
sources.quote: |tradeable = No

sources.title: Scroll of Redirection
sources.quote: |update = Nightmare Zone rewards

facts.caveat: 'Only from NMZ' rests on the page describing the scroll as a Nightmare Zone reward; its shop list is generated dynamically and was not visible in wikitext. NMZ is UNSAFE on Hardcore Worlds (C-LOG-003). Cited revision re-fetched and the current revision fetched the same day: the current revision is the cited one (no change).

facts.subject: Magic carpet
facts.value: Shantay Pass to Pollnivneach, 200 coins
facts.statement: Magic carpets from Shantay Pass to Pollnivneach cost 200 coins per trip (100 with Ring of Charos (a) or after starting Rogue Trader).

sources.title: Magic carpet
sources.quote: The carpets require 200 [[coins]] to use, but this falls to 100 coins when using the [[Ring of Charos(a)]] or after having started the [[Rogue Trader]] miniquest. If both conditions are met, the price is reduced to 75 coins.

sources.title: Pollnivneach
sources.quote: *[[Shantay Pass]] to Pollnivneach or back

facts.subject: Shantay Pass
facts.value: bank chest at Shantay Pass (members); pass costs 5 coins
facts.statement: Shantay Pass has a members' bank chest, so with the carpet it is the practical bank for the Pollnivneach course; entering the desert needs a 5-coin Shantay pass.

sources.title: Shantay Pass
sources.quote: The Shantay Pass has a [[bank chest]] which players can access before entering the desert. The bank is only available to members, but the [[Bank Deposit Box|deposit box]] is available in [[free-to-play]].

sources.title: Shantay Pass
sources.quote: Players will need to have 5 coins to buy a [[shantay pass (item)|pass]] from [[Shantay]], or have completed the elite [[Desert Diary]], if they wish to enter the desert.

sources.title: Pollnivneach
sources.quote: *[[Banknote Exchange Merchant]]

facts.caveat: 'Practical bank for Pollnivneach' is the desk's reading: the town page lists only a Banknote Exchange Merchant. Whether the carpet ride itself needs the Shantay pass item was not checked. Cited revision re-fetched and the current revision fetched the same day: the current revision is the cited one (no change).

facts.subject: Pollnivneach Rooftop Course
facts.statement: Pollnivneach is not affected by desert heat, so no waterskins are needed for the course.

sources.title: Pollnivneach Rooftop Course
sources.quote: Pollnivneach is not affected by [[desert heat]], so no waterskins are required.

facts.caveat: The town page adds that the area south of town does have desert heat. Cited revision re-fetched and the current revision fetched the same day: the current revision is the cited one (no change).

facts.subject: Pollnivneach
facts.value: crocodiles (63, aggressive) south of town; jackals aggressive to combat 42 or lower
facts.statement: In Pollnivneach the bandits and Menaphite thugs are not aggressive, but aggressive level 63 crocodiles live south of town, and jackals south-west are aggressive to combat level 42 or lower.

sources.title: Pollnivneach
sources.quote: *[[Crocodile]]s - Crocodiles populate the area south of town and may be dangerous to lower levelled players as their combat level is 63. They are aggressive. It should be noted that the area south of town has the [[Desert heat|effects]] of the desert and, unlike town, water is required in the form of [[waterskin]]s.

sources.title: Pollnivneach
sources.quote: *[[Jackal]]s - Slightly south-west of the Menaphite tent, next to the crocodiles, is a pack of jackals. These are aggressive to players with a combat level of 42 or less and can wander into areas affected by [[Desert heat]].

facts.caveat: Director correction (ledger seq 49): owner combat level is 45, so per this page the jackals (aggressive to 42 or less) would NOT be aggressive to the owner; the level 63 crocodiles remain aggressive. Thugs and bandits are non-aggressive. Hazard rating belongs to the Threat desk. Cited revision re-fetched and the current revision fetched the same day: the current revision is the cited one (no change).

facts.subject: Rellekka teleport
facts.value: untradeable redirected tablet; needs 30 Construction
facts.statement: The Rellekka teleport tablet is untradeable and needs 30 Construction (owner has 23) plus a Nightmare Zone scroll of redirection, so it is not available to the owner.

sources.title: Rellekka teleport
sources.quote: It can be created at level 30 [[Construction]] by using a [[scroll of redirection]] on a [[teleport to house]] tablet.

sources.title: Rellekka teleport
sources.quote: |tradeable = No

facts.subject: Rellekka
facts.value: enchanted lyre needs The Fremennik Trials; Camelot Teleport is a very long run
facts.statement: The enchanted lyre (closest teleport) needs The Fremennik Trials (not completed); Camelot Teleport works but leaves a very long run north.

sources.title: Rellekka teleport
sources.quote: It is extremely close to the [[enchanted lyre]] teleport location (requires completion of The Fremennik Trials).

sources.title: Rellekka
sources.quote: * {{Plink|Camelot Teleport}} — Camelot, a very long run south of the village.

sources.title: Rellekka
sources.quote: Players can [[mooring point|dock]] at Rellekka with level 62 [[Sailing]], provided they have also completed [[The Fremmenik Trials]].

facts.caveat: Owner has 44 Magic, so 'Camelot Teleport works' means the tablet (C-LOG-077), not the spell (45). The Rellekka page also shows Sailing docking needs 62 Sailing plus The Fremennik Trials (owner Sailing 30), so a boat is not an option now. Other listed teleports were not checked against the owner's unlocks. Cited revision re-fetched and the current revision fetched the same day: the current revision is the cited one (no change).

facts.subject: Rellekka
facts.value: no bank in Rellekka; Peer the Seer deposit box after Easy Fremennik diary
facts.statement: Rellekka lacks a nearby bank; Peer the Seer acts as a deposit box only after the Easy Fremennik diary.

sources.title: Rellekka
sources.quote: * {{Chatl|Peer the Seer}}, a seer who can see the future and can also help you make [[Skeletal armour]]. After completion of the [[Fremennik Diary#Easy|Easy Fremennik Diary]] he acts as a bank deposit box.

sources.title: Rellekka
sources.quote: * To the north-east of the longhall is a [[mining]] area containing seven [[coal]], four [[clay]], and three [[silver rocks]] though this spot is not recommended due to the lack of a nearby bank.

facts.caveat: 'No bank in Rellekka' is inferred from absence: the town page lists no bank, and the Sailing dock utilities list (Shipwright, Notice board, Salvaging station, Ledger table) has none. Nearest full bank still not established. Cited revision re-fetched and the current revision fetched the same day: the current revision is the cited one (no change).

facts.subject: Ardougne teleport (tablet)
facts.value: GE-tradeable; needs Plague City (completed)
facts.statement: Ardougne teleport tablets are GE-tradeable and need Plague City (which the owner has); the spell itself needs 51 Magic (owner has 44), so tablets are the owner's route.

sources.title: Ardougne teleport (tablet)
sources.quote: The '''Ardougne teleport''' is a [[magic tablet]] that can be broken by players to [[Teleportation|teleport]] to [[East Ardougne]]. Using the tablet requires completion of [[Plague City]], however, players '''do not''' have to read the [[Ardougne teleport scroll]] to use the tablet.

sources.title: Ardougne teleport (tablet)
sources.quote: |exchange = Yes

sources.title: Ardougne Teleport
sources.quote: |level = 51

facts.caveat: Plague City is in the owner's quest list; owner Magic 44 < 51. Cited revision re-fetched and the current revision fetched the same day: the current revision is the cited one (no change).

facts.subject: Ardougne Rooftop Course
facts.value: Ardougne Teleport lands in the market centre; course starts in the market's south-east corner
facts.statement: Ardougne Teleport lands in the centre of Ardougne Market, and the course starts at the wooden beams by the gem stall in the market's south-east corner.

sources.title: East Ardougne
sources.quote: The [[Ardougne Teleport]] spell teleports the caster into the centre of the Ardougne Marketplace.

sources.title: Ardougne Rooftop Course
sources.quote: It can be started by climbing the Wooden Beams outside of the house next to the [[Ardougne Gem Stall.|gem stall]] in the south-east corner of the marketplace.

sources.title: Ardougne Teleport
sources.quote: '''Ardougne Teleport''' teleports the caster to [[East Ardougne]] [[Ardougne Market|market]].

facts.caveat: The claim is about the spell (owner cannot cast it, Magic 44). The tablet page says only 'East Ardougne'; that the tablet lands at the same market tile is assumed, not stated. Cited revision re-fetched and the current revision fetched the same day: the current revision is the cited one (no change).

facts.subject: East Ardougne
facts.value: banks near the north entrance and near the docks (south bank)
facts.statement: East Ardougne has banks near the north entrance and near the docks (the southern bank).

sources.title: East Ardougne
sources.quote: Near the main north entrance of Ardougne and near the docks of Ardougne is a [[bank]]. Here, items can be stored to keep them safe when you die, and for being able to carry more.

facts.caveat: Distance from the course start was not measured. Cited revision re-fetched and the current revision fetched the same day: the current revision is the cited one (no change).

facts.subject: East Ardougne
facts.statement: A lever near the West Ardougne gate teleports the player to the Deserted Keep in deep Wilderness; avoid it.

sources.title: East Ardougne
sources.quote: *A [[Ardougne teleport lever|Teleport Lever]] - near the gates to [[West Ardougne]], there is a small house. It teleports the player to the [[Deserted Keep]] in deep [[Wilderness]] (or vice versa).

facts.caveat: Hazard: flag for the Threat desk. Cited revision re-fetched and the current revision fetched the same day: the current revision is the cited one (no change).

facts.subject: Canifis Rooftop Course
facts.value: starts just north of Canifis bank
facts.statement: The Canifis course (needs Priest in Peril, completed) starts at the Tall Tree just north of the bank and ends on the bank's north side.

sources.title: Canifis Rooftop Course
sources.quote: The Canifis Rooftop Agility Course can be started by climbing the Tall Tree just north of the [[bank]] and is finished by jumping off the north side of the bank.

sources.title: Canifis Rooftop Course
sources.quote: It is only accessible to players who have completed the [[Priest in Peril]] quest.

facts.caveat: Priest in Peril is in the owner's quest list. Cited revision re-fetched and the current revision fetched the same day: the current revision is the cited one (no change).

facts.subject: Ectophial
facts.value: free reusable teleport to the Ectofuntus (far east of Canifis); reward of Ghosts Ahoy
facts.statement: The ectophial (Ghosts Ahoy reward, completed) is a free, reusable, untradeable teleport to the Ectofuntus outside Port Phasmatys, which is far east of Canifis.

sources.title: Ectophial
sources.quote: The '''ectophial''' is a reward for completing the [[Ghosts Ahoy]] quest. Players can empty it, causing them to be teleported to the [[Ectofuntus]] outside [[Port Phasmatys]]. Once the player teleports, they will automatically refill it.

sources.title: Ectophial
sources.quote: |tradeable = No

sources.title: Canifis
sources.quote: * {{Plink|Ectophial}} — [[Ectofuntus]], far east of the town.

facts.caveat: Ghosts Ahoy is in the owner's quest list. Cited revision re-fetched and the current revision fetched the same day: the current revision is the cited one (no change).

facts.statement: The Colossal Wyrm course needs Children of the Sun (completed) and 50 Agility (basic) or 62 (advanced).

sources.title: Colossal Wyrm Agility Course
sources.quote: There are two courses available to players beginning at 50 Agility for the basic course, and 62 Agility for the advanced course.

sources.title: Colossal Wyrm Agility Course

facts.caveat: Infobox requirement list: Children of the Sun, 50 (Basic), 62 (Advanced). Children of the Sun is in the owner's quest list. The page's Obsolete banner covers durations/XP/termites, not requirements. Cited revision re-fetched and the current revision fetched the same day: the current revision is the cited one (no change).

facts.subject: Colossal wyrm teleport scroll
facts.value: GE-tradeable or 40 termites; usable after visiting Varlamore post-Children of the Sun
facts.statement: Colossal wyrm teleport scrolls (fastest way to the course) are GE-tradeable or cost 40 termites from Worm Tongue, and work once the player has visited Varlamore after Children of the Sun.

sources.title: Colossal wyrm teleport scroll
sources.quote: They can be purchased from [[Worm Tongue's Wares]] for 40 [[termites]] obtained from the [[Colossal Wyrm Agility Course]].

sources.title: Colossal wyrm teleport scroll

sources.title: Colossal Wyrm Agility Course
sources.quote: * Use a [[Colossal wyrm teleport scroll]], bought from [[Worm Tongue]] or the [[Grand Exchange]]. This is the quickest method to get there.

facts.statement: Quetzal landing sites, including the one near the Colossal Wyrm Remains, are only usable after Twilight's Promise (not completed) and must be built from 10 quetzal feed, 3 limestone bricks and 4 soft clay.

sources.quote: {{Obsolete|Changes to course durations, experience, termites, and bone shards.|update=Update:Summer Sweep Up - Agility & Chambers of Xeric Changes}}

facts.subject: Wilderness Agility Course
facts.value: Ice plateau tablet (lands in level 53 Wilderness) or Wilderness obelisk/Edgeville lever
facts.statement: The fastest way to the Wilderness course is an Ice plateau teleport tablet (no requirements to use, GE-tradeable) to level 53 Wilderness, then run east; banking is via the obelisk to Ferox Enclave.

sources.title: Ice plateau teleport (tablet)
sources.quote: The '''Ice plateau teleport''' is a [[magic tablet]] that can be broken by players to [[Teleportation|teleport]] to the members half of the [[Ice Plateau]] in level 53 [[Wilderness]].

sources.title: Ice plateau teleport (tablet)
sources.quote: |exchange = Yes

sources.title: Wilderness Agility Course
sources.quote: |[[Ice Plateau Teleport]] spell or [[Ice plateau teleport (tablet)|tablet]]<ref group="a">The tablet has no requirements to use.</ref>

sources.title: Wilderness Agility Course
sources.quote: Players can generally assume a lap time of 45 seconds. Bank time is assumed to be 2 minutes, 10 seconds, and done by leaving the course, running through the gate to the Wilderness obelisk, traveling to the 13-Wilderness option (Ferox Enclave), using the bank, and then returning with an [[Ice plateau teleport (tablet)|Ice Plateau tablet]].

facts.caveat: Deep Wilderness/PvP: Threat desk. Tablets are made at 89 Magic on the Lunar spellbook; Hardcore Worlds supply unknown. Other listed routes: Wilderness obelisk (to 44 Wilderness), burning amulet (Lava Maze), Edgeville lever (needs a knife or slash weapon for the web). Cited revision re-fetched and the current revision fetched the same day: the current revision is the cited one (no change).

facts.subject: Wilderness Agility Course
facts.statement: The Wilderness course's optional loot fee is 150,000 coins, paid from the inventory and lost on every death or exit; without it the course is free but gives no loot.

sources.title: Wilderness Agility Course
sources.quote: The fee is 150,000 coins, which is lost '''every time''' a player dies or leaves the course, but is not removed if they log out and remain within the course. '''This money must be deposited from a player's inventory''', unlike other Wilderness fees which can be withdrawn from a bank.

facts.subject: Brimhaven Agility Arena
facts.statement: Brimhaven Agility Arena charges 200 coins per entry, and logging out inside means paying again.

sources.title: Brimhaven Agility Arena
sources.quote: *Bring 200 [[coins]] to pay [[Cap'n Izzy No-Beard]] for access to the arena. It is recommended to bring more, as this fee has to be paid upon each entry. Logging out while in the arena will throw you out and require you to pay the fee again. You will need to wait at least a minute before being allowed to re-enter.

facts.subject: Brimhaven Agility Arena
facts.value: boat from East Ardougne or Rimmington; charter ship; glory to Musa Point
facts.statement: To reach Brimhaven Agility Arena, take the boat from East Ardougne or Rimmington, a charter ship, or an amulet of glory to Musa Point and run west.

sources.title: Brimhaven Agility Arena
sources.quote: *Take the boat from [[East Ardougne]] or [[Rimmington]] to Brimhaven or alternatively take a [[charter ship]].

sources.title: Brimhaven Agility Arena
sources.quote: *Teleport to [[Musa Point]] using an [[amulet of glory]] and run west.

facts.caveat: The page also lists a Fight Cave minigame-teleport route through Mor Ul Rek; the TzHaar Fight Cave itself is UNSAFE on Hardcore Worlds (Threat desk). Cited revision re-fetched and the current revision fetched the same day: the current revision is the cited one (no change).

facts.subject: Brimhaven Agility Arena
facts.value: small-heal food or summer pies; energy-restoring items needed
facts.statement: At Brimhaven bring food (summer pies, or small heals like chocolate cake or strawberries, because trap damage scales with current HP) and enough energy-restoring items to run constantly.

sources.title: Brimhaven Agility Arena
sources.quote: **Food that heals in small increments such as [[chocolate cake]]s or [[strawberries|baskets of strawberries]] are another good choice, as the damage the traps deal to your health scale with how much health you currently have. By keeping your health around 20, the traps deal the least amount of damage, which is easier to maintain when healing by smaller amounts.

sources.title: Brimhaven Agility Arena
sources.quote: **[[Summer pie]]s are recommended, as those restore run energy and boost the Agility stat by +5, which is useful since the darts obstacle will drain the Agility stat by 2 levels upon failing.

sources.title: Brimhaven Agility Arena
sources.quote: *Bring enough [[Energy#Energy-restoring action|energy-restoring items]] for enough [[energy]] to constantly run around the course.

facts.caveat: No per-hour quantities in any source. The page's 'keep health around 20' advice is a Hardcore risk question for the Threat desk. Cited revision re-fetched and the current revision fetched the same day: the current revision is the cited one (no change).

facts.subject: Brimhaven Agility Arena
facts.value: Karamja gloves 2/3/4: +10% obstacle and ticket XP
facts.statement: Karamja gloves 2, 3 or 4 give 10% extra Brimhaven obstacle and ticket XP (they need the Karamja diary, which the owner does not have).

sources.title: Brimhaven Agility Arena
sources.quote: *Wear [[Karamja gloves 2]], [[Karamja gloves 3|3]], or [[Karamja gloves 4|4]] for 10% extra Agility experience from obstacles in the Brimhaven Agility Arena.

sources.title: Brimhaven Agility Arena
sources.quote: *Bring [[Karamja gloves 2]], [[Karamja gloves 3|3]], or [[Karamja gloves 4|4]] when turning in tickets for the 10% experience bonus.

facts.caveat: Dispenser-tag XP is not boosted by the gloves (same page). Owner has no diaries. Cited revision re-fetched and the current revision fetched the same day: the current revision is the cited one (no change).

facts.subject: Agility Pyramid
facts.value: waterskins (desert heat) and food; fails deal up to 10 damage
facts.statement: The Agility Pyramid is in desert heat, so bring waterskins and food (unless Desert Elite diary); falls deal up to 10 damage.

sources.title: Agility Pyramid
sources.quote: Players will suffer from [[desert heat]] while in this area. Those who have completed the [[Desert Diary#Elite|elite Desert Diary]] can wear the [[desert amulet 4]] for complete protection from the heat. Otherwise, players will need to bring enough [[waterskin]]s and [[food]] for the training.

sources.title: Agility Pyramid
sources.quote: Upon failure, the Agility Pyramid is capable of hitting a player for 10 damage, so [[Ironman Mode#Hardcore|hardcore ironmen]] should be wary.

facts.caveat: The page says a fail can hit 10; whether 10 is the maximum ('up to') is not stated. Cited revision re-fetched and the current revision fetched the same day: the current revision is the cited one (no change).

facts.subject: Agility Pyramid
facts.value: magic carpet Shantay Pass→Pollnivneach→Nardah, then walk
facts.statement: One route without diaries: carpet from Shantay Pass to Pollnivneach, then a carpet to Nardah and walk south-west to the pyramid.

sources.title: Agility Pyramid
sources.quote: * Alternatively, take a magic carpet from [[Shantay Pass]] to Pollnivneach and follow the instructions above.

sources.title: Agility Pyramid
sources.quote: ** Take a magic carpet to [[Nardah]] and walk south-west from Nardah.

facts.caveat: One of several listed routes (others: Nardah teleport, fairy ring DLQ (needs fairy rings), ferry from Al Kharid to the Ruins of Unkah). The walk from Nardah is in desert heat; the 'run south from Pollnivneach' variant passes the aggressive crocodiles (C-LOG-084). Cited revision re-fetched and the current revision fetched the same day: the current revision is the cited one (no change).

facts.subject: Agility Pyramid
facts.value: pyramid top sold to Simon Templeton for 10,000 coins
facts.statement: Each pyramid top sells to Simon Templeton for 10,000 coins (up to about 26 tops/hour); sell each one at once because it weighs 11 kg.

sources.title: Agility Pyramid
sources.quote: Pyramid tops may be handed in to [[Simon Templeton]] in exchange for {{NoCoins|10,000}} [[coins]] each and respawn only when the player has entered the doorway at the top of the pyramid.

sources.title: Agility Pyramid
sources.quote: Players are advised to sell each pyramid top to Simon Templeton immediately after obtaining it, since it weighs 11 kg and would otherwise increase run energy expenditure on future laps.

sources.title: Agility Pyramid
sources.quote: Level 75 Agility or higher ensures success on all of the obstacles, making it possible to complete a maximum of 26 laps per hour, which rewards a maximum of 44,700 experience per hour.

facts.caveat: 26 tops/hour is a maximum at 75+ Agility. Cited revision re-fetched and the current revision fetched the same day: the current revision is the cited one (no change).

facts.subject: Werewolf Agility Course
facts.value: Creature of Fenkenstrain + Ring of Charos
facts.statement: The Werewolf Agility Course needs Creature of Fenkenstrain (not completed) and a Ring of Charos, so the owner cannot use it.

sources.title: Agility training
sources.quote: To access this course, players must have completed [[Creature of Fenkenstrain]] and wear a [[Ring of Charos]].

sources.title: Werewolf Agility Course

facts.subject: The Fremennik Trials: Koschei the deathless, forms 1-3
facts.value: UNSAFE_DEATH
facts.statement: On Hardcore Worlds a death to Koschei's first, second or third form is an unsafe (run-ending) death. Both Jagex Hardcore Worlds posts list only 'The Fremennik Trials (only the 4th phase of the duel with Koschei the Deathless)' as safe; Hardcore Worlds uses the Hardcore Group Ironman death ruleset. The wiki's Koschei and Fremennik Trials pages say forms 1-3 are safe for regular Hardcore Ironmen, which does not apply here.
facts.caveat: Hardcore Worlds launched 2026-11-04 (16 days before verification): new content whose rules Jagex may still revise; re-check the T1 posts before publishing. The wiki pages contain HCIM-safe wording for forms 1-3 (Koschei rev 15387641 line 226; Fremennik Trials rev 15396092 line 218) that planners must not use. Default UNSAFE applies.

facts.subject: Hardcore Worlds safe-death exceptions

t1_safe_list: The Fremennik Trials (only the 4th phase of the duel with Koschei the Deathless)
TzHaar Fight Caves Resurrection reward (Karamja Elite Diary)
Zulrah (only the Resurrection reward from the Elite Western Provinces Diary)
wiki_hw_page_adds: Capsizing your Boat (other deaths on a boat unsafe)

facts.statement: Both Jagex Hardcore Worlds posts list exactly seven safe exceptions; the only quest fight among them is Koschei's 4th phase. The wiki's Hardcore Worlds page lists those seven too (Soul Wars, TzHaar Fight Pit and the Zulrah resurrection are its lines 61-63) and adds six items with no T1 backing: boat capsizing, Emir's Arena, Last Man Standing (disabled at launch), Pete Kayer's Challenges, and the Galvek and Glough replays. Treat those six as UNSAFE until Jagex confirms them.
facts.caveat: Correction, not a value change: the researcher's statement says the wiki page 'leaves out Soul Wars, TzHaar Fight Pit and the Zulrah resurrection'. My fetch of the same revision (15404671, unchanged today) shows all three listed as SAFE, so that sentence is wrong; the value itself is right. New content (launched 2026-11-04). Last Man Standing cannot be accessed on Hardcore Worlds (OUT TODAY line 217).

facts.subject: Koschei the deathless (The Fremennik Trials)
facts.statement: Koschei's max hits are 3 / 5 / 7 for forms 1-3, each attacking every 4 ticks (2.4 s), with 30 / 50 / 70 Hitpoints. Form 4 hits for at most 1 but every tick (0.6 s), has 255 Hitpoints and 255 Attack: up to 100 damage per minute (computed: 60 s / 0.6 s = 100 hits x 1).
facts.caveat: Second confirmation is partial: the 3/5/7 values appear only on the Koschei page (infobox and its strategy prose, same page); the Fremennik Trials page independently confirms only form 4's 1 damage per tick. No non-wiki source was found. One Koschei-page sentence ('in his third and fourth form he hits progressively harder and quicker') does not match the infobox.

sources.title: Koschei the deathless
sources.quote: His max hits are 3 in his first form, 5 in his second, and 7 in his third.

sources.title: Koschei the deathless
sources.quote: *He is the fastest attacking [[NPC]] in the game (in his final form with an attack speed of 1, meaning every 0.6 seconds), along with [[Scarab swarm]]s. The attack speed for his first three forms is 4 (2.4 seconds), the same as unarmed combat.

sources.title: The Fremennik Trials
sources.quote: The fourth form is the hardest. He will hit once every game tick, but can only hit for 1 damage at a time.

facts.subject: Koschei the deathless, form 4
facts.statement: When Koschei's 4th form starts he drains all your prayer points, then keeps draining them by 1-2 every second, so protection prayers cannot be relied on in form 4.
facts.caveat: Single source for the exact rates (Fremennik Trials walkthrough). The Koschei page change log (6 February 2014: 'Koschei now keeps it drained') supports the drain but gives no numbers.

sources.title: The Fremennik Trials
sources.quote: In this form, Koschei will quickly drop your prayer points in intervals of 1-2 every second and will drop all of your prayer points as soon as the form starts.

sources.title: Koschei the deathless
sources.quote: |change = After Koschei the Deathless drained your prayer in [[Fremennik Trials]], players could simply restore it and re-activate their prayers. Koschei now keeps it drained.

facts.subject: The Fremennik Trials: Koschei fight arena

value.ring_of_life: teleports you to your respawn point and the fight restarts at form 1
value.phase_timer: 10 minutes in one phase, then Koschei despawns and the fight resets
value.walk_out: not documented (a ladder is mentioned only in an untested aside)

facts.statement: The Koschei fight is in an instance under Thorvald's house. Weapons, armour, fletching materials and runes are not allowed; food, Prayer, god books and jewellery are. A ring of life sends you to your respawn point and you restart at form 1. Spending 10 minutes in one phase makes Koschei disappear and the fight restart. Whether normal teleports or walking out work mid-fight is not documented.

sources.title: Koschei the deathless
sources.quote: Additionally, if you take too long fighting Koschei (10 minutes in the same phase), he will simply disappear and you will have to start the challenge all over again.

facts.subject: The Fremennik Trials: Koschei fight arena
facts.value: Koschei can be trapped on the far side of a chasm or by the pillars of fire to regenerate. Staying too long makes him reset to form 1. He can be flinched at the torches.
facts.statement: There is no attack safespot (you have no weapons), but you can trap Koschei on the other side of a hole in the floor or by the fire pillars and regenerate. Staying too long makes him disappear and come back in form 1. He can also be flinched from the north or south tile of a torch.

sources.title: The Fremennik Trials
sources.quote: There is no way to safespot him as you have no weapons, but you can trap him over the hole and wait a while for your health to regenerate. However, if you stay there too long, he will disappear and reappear after you run around, back in his first form.

sources.title: Koschei the deathless
sources.quote: It is possible to [[flinch]] Koschei by standing on either the south or north tile of one of the torches in the room while Koschei is east or west of the same torch.

facts.subject: The Writing's on the Wall

value.guards: being caught sends you back to the cell (no damage documented)

facts.statement: The Writing's on the Wall has no fights (empty kills field); the trapdoor-room ambush is a cutscene. You cannot teleport out of the Port Piscarilius prison cell ('A teleport block has been placed on this cell'); you escape by removing a plank and climbing through the gap in the north wall. Being caught by either jail guard sends you straight back to the cell.

facts.subject: Underground Pass: traps and environment

value.wall_trap_run_through: percentage of current HP (as low as 3); standing in front repeatedly hits very fast and could be fatal
value.iban_spikes: about 5-8 each, rapid, not blocked by prayer, stun and send you back to the entrance
value.teleport: instant teleports work to leave the dungeon
value.death_penalty_note: dying during the doll step means running the whole dungeon again

facts.statement: Underground Pass damage outside fights: grid-puzzle pits always deal 15; wall traps 5-14 on a failed disarm; running through a wall trap hits a percentage of current HP (as low as 3), and standing in front of an armed trap 'will repeatedly hit very fast and could be fatal'; swinging logs 6-13; a failed Iban's Lair bridge jump deals 'up to 24 (20% + 5)' and lands you among Soulless; Iban's tomb claw 10; Iban's red spikes about 5-8 each, rapid, not blocked by prayer, with stun and return to the entrance. Any instant teleport can be used to leave. Dying during the doll step means running the whole dungeon again.
facts.caveat: The bridge figure is internally inconsistent ('up to 24' vs '20% + 5', which is about 14-15 at the owner's 48 Hitpoints); use 24 as the conservative bound. Bridge success is about 39% at Agility 1 rising linearly to 100% at 77 (Mod Ash via Bridge rev 15401279); computed for the owner's Agility 57: 39 + 56 x (117-39)/98 = about 84% per jump, so falls are likely over many jumps.

sources.title: Underground Pass
sources.quote: The grid puzzle '''always''' does 15 damage upon falling into a pit. ... #The traps can be disarmed normally, with a chance to fail and be hit for 5 to 14 damage. #Run through the traps one at a time, which hits a percentage of your current health, as low as 3.

sources.title: Underground Pass
sources.quote: Disarming can be failed, triggering a swinging log, dealing 6 to 13 damage. ... a yellow claw will hit you for 10 damage. ... These spikes rapidly deal around 5 to 8 damage each and can't be blocked with prayers.

sources.title: Bridge (Iban's Lair)

value.reset: recovers to full HP if the fight takes too long; leave and re-enter to retry

facts.statement: Once a flashback in Icthlarin's Little Helper begins you cannot teleport away until you finish it or die. The second-flashback guardian is an apparition: Het (81, max hit 9, Slash), Apmeken (75, max hit 6, Magic) or Scabaras (75, max hit 8, Slash); Crondis (75, max hit 6, Magic) is not used for quests started after 27 April 2022. Your canopic jar decides which one, weighted by your highest of Attack/Strength, Ranged or Magic plus equipment bonuses at quest start; examine the jar before the pit jump to know.
facts.caveat: Correction to the researcher's statement ('one of four apparitions'): the quest page's jar table marks Crondis 'Unused, unless the quest was started prior to 27 April 2022', and the Apparition page says Crondis will not appear for quests started after that date, so only three are possible for a new start. The owner's highest combat stat is Ranged 56 (brief), which makes Apmeken (Magic) most likely, but not certain. The page also says logging out during a flashback places you outside the pyramid entrance, a non-teleport exit (normal logout rules in combat still apply). Klenter's Pyramid also has wall crushers, pit traps, mummies (84) and scarab swarms (2 damage plus poison); crusher damage is not quantified.

facts.subject: Monkey Madness I: Ape Atoll Dungeon tunnel (Chapter 2)

value.teleport: teleport out recommended at the end

facts.statement: The Ape Atoll Dungeon is a long, tight multicombat tunnel with 30 aggressive monkey zombies (max hit 7) and 17 gorilla skeletons (level 142). The skeleton's max hit is 10 in its infobox but 12 in the quest guide: use 12. Floor spikes deal 7.5% of current HP rapidly, the rock trap 20%, falling rocks 4% every 15 s (all rounded up). It takes at least three minutes of running. You go through at least twice: for the enchanted bar, then to have Zooknock make greegrees. The guide says to teleport out at the end.
facts.caveat: The value records an unresolved source conflict: Skeleton (Ape Atoll) infobox max hit 10 (rev 15322119, unchanged) vs 12 in the Monkey Madness I prose and threats table. No third source found; planners and the Risk Officer must use 12. The Monkey Zombie page is internally inconsistent on the tunnel level (location table: Ape Atoll Dungeon level 98; prose: level 98 only in the Temple of Marimbo skull room); max hit is 7 for both level 82 and level 98, so the max hit is unaffected.

facts.subject: Agility-XP quest prerequisite chains
facts.statement: Fixed Defence XP from the listed not-yet-done prerequisite quests: 0 for the Troll, Elf, Cabin Fever, Heart of Darkness and Land of the Goblins chains; 4,600 for the Myreque chain (Defence 20); 24,537.4 for the Royal Trouble chain (Fremennik Trials 2,812.4 + Heroes' Quest 3,075 + Dragon Slayer I 18,650; Defence 35); 29,137.4 for both (Defence 37) and 31,137.4 with What Lies Below (Defence 38). All are below 111,945 XP, the threshold of Defence 51, so these quests alone keep the owner within the Defence 50 cap.
facts.caveat: Every per-quest number re-fetched (rewards boxes and the Defence table, incl. The Fremennik Trials 2,812.4) and the sums and levels recomputed with tools/xp.py (4,600 -> 20; 24,537.4 -> 35; 29,137.4 -> 37; 31,137.4 -> 38; level 51 = 111,945). The chains contain only the quests named in the value: quest-point requirements (e.g. Heroes' Quest needs 55 QP) and deeper prerequisites (Curse of Arrav/Defender of Varrock, Dragon Slayer II, Recipe for Disaster) were not traced, and could force further Defence-XP quests (e.g. Holy Grail 15,300, Olaf's Quest 12,000). Choosable lamps and optional training are excluded and must never go to Defence.

facts.subject: Shield of Arrav

value.partner_already_done: may help only if they chose to obtain extra certificate halves before completing

facts.statement: Shield of Arrav cannot be fully completed alone: it needs a partner who picks the opposing gang. A partner who already finished can help only if they also picked the opposing gang and obtained extra certificate halves first. The key and certificate halves can be used on the partner instead of traded. The wiki points to the official chat-channel 'OSRS SOA' to find a partner.

If your partner has already fully completed the quest, they may only assist if they both picked the opposing gang and chose to obtain additional [[certificate half|certificate halves]] before completing the quest.

facts.subject: Hardcore Worlds

value.implication: a Shield of Arrav / Heroes' Quest partner must be another Hardcore Worlds character (inference)

facts.statement: Hardcore Worlds run on servers separate from the standard worlds, but its characters are main accounts that can trade with other players and do group PvM. A quest partner therefore has to be another Hardcore Worlds character playing on a Hardcore world (inference).
facts.caveat: The three mode facts are sourced (wiki HW page; Jagex launch post: HW items can only be bought and sold within those worlds). That a main-game character cannot partner a Hardcore Worlds character is an inference from the separate servers; no source states it. Whether the 'OSRS SOA' chat-channel or the Grouping interface reaches HW players is undocumented. New content (HW launched 2026-11-04).

facts.caveat: Candidates confirmed; nearness is not measured by any source. The Keldagrim entrance mine page names Keldagrim as the nearest bank to that mine only. Hazards in the Keldagrim tunnel and on the route were not researched. 'No bank in Rellekka' rests on C-LOG-087 and the Rellekka page's remark that its mine lacks a nearby bank.

facts.subject: Ferox Enclave
facts.value: PvP-safe town inside level 13-16 Wilderness; ring of dueling teleports directly into it without crossing the Wilderness; leaving through the barriers puts you in the PvP Wilderness, which Hardcore Worlds keeps
facts.statement: Ferox Enclave is a town in level 13-16 Wilderness where players cannot kill other players. A ring of dueling (GE-tradeable at 8 charges) teleports straight in, without crossing the Wilderness; the bank is a few tiles from the pools. Tele-blocked players cannot enter through the barriers. Outside the barriers is the PvP Wilderness, which Hardcore Worlds keeps (Jagex: death proceeds as normal there).
facts.caveat: The wiki describes the main game; no Hardcore-Worlds-specific source confirms the Ferox safe zone behaves identically on HW worlds. HW content is new (launched 2026-11-04). Stay inside and leave by teleport.

Both have right-click 'Inside' and 'Outside' options (the tablet also 'Group'); left-click follows the inside/outside setting in house options, and the default can also be Building Mode (still inside). facts.value: UNSAFE_DEATH
facts.statement: A death on any rooftop course, on the Colossal Wyrm course or in the Hallowed Sepulchre is an official (run-ending) death on Hardcore Worlds. Hardcore Worlds use the Hardcore Group Ironman death ruleset, and none of these activities is on Jagex's safe list or the wiki's current Hardcore Worlds safe list. No Update post from 4 to 20 November 2026 adds them. The Sepulchre's item retention is an ordinary death mechanic, not a safe-death rule.
facts.caveat: T1-backed: Jagex's safe list (Castle Wars, Clan Wars, Soul Wars, Fremennik Trials 4th Koschei phase, Fight Caves and Zulrah resurrection rewards, TzHaar Fight Pit) contains no Agility activity, and the wiki's current safe list (adds boat capsizing, Emir's Arena, LMS, Pete Kayer's Challenges, Galvek and Glough replays) contains none either. Hardcore Worlds launched 2026-11-04 (new content); recheck the safe list before publishing.

facts.statement: In the Underground Pass a failed north rope swing deals up to 14 damage, the rope is lost, and you must climb back to the very start of the Pass. A failed Iban's Lair bridge jump deals up to 24 (20% + 5) and drops you among the Soulless; bridge success runs from about 39% at level 1 to 100% at 77 (about 83.6% per jump at Agility 57, computed). The swamp always fails and the ledge sends you back through the slave cage. All obstacles are possible at level 1.
facts.caveat: Rope swing, bridge, ledge, swamp and level-1 statements confirmed. Computed values: 39 + 78 x 56/98 = 83.6% (Mod Ash's 39%/117% line). The '20% + 5' basis is not stated as current or max HP; 'about 14' for the owner assumes 20% of 48 HP plus 5 with unknown rounding. The swamp's 'hillside' wording comes from the dungeon page's music note ('the hillside rocky pit when falling through the swamp or rope swing'); no swamp damage is stated. Many jumps are needed, so at least one fall is likely.
